What share of the text is emoji, and is it emoji-only?

Source: R/emoji-metrics.R
emoji_ratio.Rd

emoji_ratio() reports, per row, the share of the text's characters that belong to emoji, and whether the text is emoji-only (nothing left after removing emoji and whitespace). "Emoji-only" messages are a studied signal in social-media research and a useful filter in practice.

Usage

emoji_ratio(data, text, presentation = "emoji")

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble containing a text column. Grouped data frames are accepted. The verbs that work a row at a time (adding columns, or keeping and expanding rows) carry the grouping through to their result, as dplyr::mutate() and dplyr::filter() do. The verbs that pool across rows – the counts, the co-occurrence edge lists, the time series – warn that they ignore the grouping and return one corpus-wide answer.

text

The text column to scan, supplied unquoted. Any atomic column is accepted and read as character, so a factor works and a numeric, Date or logical one simply contains no emoji. A list column – or a data-frame column – is refused rather than coerced, because coercing one deparses it and the emoji found would be in the code rather than in your data. What counts as an emoji is the same in every verb; see the Detection section of tidyEmoji for the one case that surprises people, code points that are emoji only when they carry U+FE0F.

presentation

Which code points count as emoji: "emoji" (the default) or "any".

  • "emoji" requires emoji presentation, so U+2764 U+FE0F is an emoji and the bare U+2764 is not. This is the default and it will stay the default: widening it would silently recount every corpus already analysed.

  • "any" also reads the text-presentation spellings Unicode lists for an emoji (the bare heart, U+263A, U+2714, a keycap without its selector), because several keyboards emit them. It never reads the copyright, registered and trade-mark signs (U+00A9, U+00AE, U+2122), which are typography far more often than they are emoji.

"any" only ever adds occurrences: everything "emoji" finds, it finds too, in the same place. emoji_coverage() reports how many it adds and how many of those a lexicon can score, which is the cost of the choice in one number. Every verb that counts, scores or rewrites the emoji in a text column takes this argument, so counts still agree across the package for whichever value you use. The flag verbs do not need it, since a flag has no text-presentation form.

Value

data, as a tibble, with added columns .emoji_n, .emoji_codepoints (code points belonging to emoji), .emoji_n_char (all code points), .emoji_ratio (.emoji_codepoints / .emoji_n_char, 0 when there are no emoji) and .emoji_only (TRUE when the text contains emoji and nothing else but whitespace). "Whitespace" is Unicode's White_Space property, written out explicitly rather than left to the C library: it includes the no-break spaces U+00A0 and U+202F and the ideographic space U+3000, and excludes the zero-width space U+200B, which despite its name Unicode does not classify as whitespace. The same set is used everywhere the package splits or trims text, and it does not vary with the locale. NA text gets NA in both, and in .emoji_n_char, with 0 in the two emoji counts. Empty text ("") has no characters to take a share of, so .emoji_ratio is NA there too, but .emoji_only is FALSE: an empty string is not a row of emoji.

Details

The ratio is computed over characters (code points), so a multi-code-point emoji (a ZWJ family, a skin-tone sequence) contributes all of its characters. It ships with both of the counts it is the quotient of, .emoji_codepoints and .emoji_n_char, and with .emoji_n, the number of emoji those code points make up; see Rates and their denominators in tidyEmoji.

A skin-tone swatch or hair component standing alone, or a regional indicator that spells no flag, is not an emoji (see the Detection section of tidyEmoji), so it adds nothing to .emoji_n or .emoji_codepoints. It is not text either, so it does not stop a row being .emoji_only: U+1F600 U+1F3FB is one emoji, a ratio of 0.5, and emoji-only. The same holds for the joiners of a zero-width-joiner sequence Unicode does not recommend, which counts as its parts: U+1F9D1 U+200D U+1F467 is two emoji, a ratio of 2/3, and emoji-only. A symbol the catalogue does not list, followed by a stray U+FE0F, is the text it is without the selector, so U+1F600 U+2605 U+FE0F (a black star) is no more emoji-only than U+1F600 U+2605, inside a joined sequence or not.

See also

emoji_position(), emoji_density(); emoji_filter() to keep emoji-bearing rows.

Examples

df <- data.frame(text = c("\U0001f600\U0001f389", "half \U0001f600", "no"))
emoji_ratio(df, text)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   text    .emoji_n .emoji_codepoints .emoji_n_char .emoji_ratio .emoji_only
#>   <chr>      <int>             <int>         <int>        <dbl> <lgl>      
#> 1 😀🎉           2                 2             2        1     TRUE       
#> 2 half 😀        1                 1             6        0.167 FALSE      
#> 3 no             0                 0             2        0     FALSE
